title: TLS certificate expiry alerting
description:
Emit metrics and log warnings when configured TLS certificates are approaching expiry, so operators are alerted before clients start seeing certificate errors.

Why this issue exists:
TLS certificate expiry is a silent, predictable outage. The daemon loads certs at startup but never checks them again. An operator who set up a cert and forgot about it will wake up to broken clients.

Scope:
- At startup, read the NotAfter field from each configured TLS certificate (reader, transit, mail, smtp)
- Emit a structured log event at WARN if expiry is within 30 days: event=cert_expiry_warning, path, days_remaining, expires_at
- Emit at ERROR if expiry is within 7 days
- Expose a Prometheus gauge tls_cert_expiry_seconds{path=...} with the Unix timestamp of each cert's expiry
- Re-check expiry on config reload (SIGHUP / POST /admin/reload)
- Checking is read-only: the daemon never fetches or renews certs (that is certbot/ACM's job)

Acceptance criteria:
- A cert expiring in 15 days produces a WARN log event at startup and on each reload
- tls_cert_expiry_seconds gauge is present in /metrics for each configured cert
- A cert expiring in 3 days produces an ERROR log event
- No alert is emitted for certs with more than 30 days remaining
